items.title: METR: AI R&D-relevant capabilities improving rapidly and getting harder to measure
items.summary_en: METR reports that AI R&D-relevant model capabilities are improving quickly. Models are nearing performance ceilings on some tasks, so apparent progress may look slower than it is. METR adds that it is now harder to bound risk by pointing to some easy-to-measure, broad incapability.
items.notes: Direct fetch of metr.org was blocked (host not in session allowlist); based on search-result snippets of the METR page, not the full text. Methodology caveats not verified.

items.title: METR independent assessment of AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic (October 2026)
items.summary_en: METR assessed, with high-access evaluation, that Anthropic is improving its models on well-specified tasks at roughly twice its March 2024 to October 2025 rate. About 80% of the current acceleration is attributed to AI, with substantial uncertainty.
items.notes: PRE-WINDOW (published 2026-11-05, before 2026-11-11 start). Snippet-based only. METR itself states high uncertainty: it would not be surprised if true acceleration were nearer 1.3x or 3x. Related to the review item metr-2026-11-05-rd-section-risk-report-review.

items.title: METR review of 'Risks from automated R&D' section in Anthropic's August 2026 Risk Report
items.summary_en: METR reviewed Anthropic's public risk report section on automated R&D. It finds a range of reasonable acceleration estimates of 1.3 to 2.8 from the leading indicators (redacted by Anthropic) and says the public report implies more confidence than the private version. It also says evidence since the report favors continued acceleration since October 2025.
items.notes: PRE-WINDOW (2026-11-05). Snippet-based only. Possible divergence between METR and Anthropic's public framing on confidence; no Anthropic response found. Follows METR's 2026-10-20 review of the misalignment section (https://metr.org/blog/2026-10-20-misalignment-risk-report-august-2026-review/), not separately itemized.

items.title: METR note: measuring alignment eval 'tells'
items.summary_en: A METR note by Uzay Girit, Kaivu Hariharan and Leni Shor reports that AI investigator agents increasingly distinguish capability evals from alignment evals. They do so by spotting environments that seem fake or tasks that look like honeypots.
items.notes: Snippet-based only. Published in METR's 'Notes' section, which is likely less formal than full reports; caveats not verified. Suggests eval-awareness could weaken alignment evaluations.

items.title: METR conflict of interest policy updated to version 1.1
items.summary_en: METR released version 1.1 of its conflict of interest policy with clarity edits and an added recusal example.
items.notes: PRE-WINDOW by one day (2026-11-10). Date and content come from a search snippet; the PDF itself was not opened. Minor administrative update.

coverage_note: Direct fetch of metr.org failed (domain not in session network allowlist), so all items rely on search-result snippets of METR's own pages; confidence is set to primary-inferred and caveats should be verified against full texts. In-window (Nov 11-21): the Nov 16 note and Nov 20 post. Pre-window items (Nov 5, Nov 10) are included and labeled. The Nov 20 capability update and Nov 5 acceleration assessments are consistent with each other (both indicate rapid AI R&D acceleration); no contradiction with earlier METR findings was identified, though earlier-week METR items were not checked. metr.org needs to be allowed in network settings for full verification.
